scope: Research informing the living-community foundation; modern field observations inform plausible mechanisms rather than a single universal Paleolithic lifestyle.

sources.title: Co-Residence Patterns in Hunter-Gatherer Societies Show Unique Human Social Structure
sources.finding: Data from 32 societies distinguish household kinship from fluid residential membership; reported experienced band size is 28.2 ADULTS, not total residents. Both sexes can disperse or remain, and many adult co-residents are not close biological relatives.
sources.design: Several linked households per camp, mixed kin/non-kin social networks, no universal male chief or sex-locked work assignment.

sources.title: Variability in the organization and size of hunter-gatherer groups: Foragers do not live in small-scale societies
sources.finding: Residential camps, foraging parties and wider social networks are distinct scales; Martu residential membership is fluid and connected beyond a single small band.
sources.design: Communities have separately scheduled household work parties, communal activities and contacts; camp membership must not be confused with all members of a culture.

sources.title: The ecological and evolutionary energetics of hunter-gatherer residential mobility
sources.finding: Resource availability, depletion, temperature and seasonality constrain residential mobility.
sources.design: Ecology-dependent itineraries and residence duration; dependable aquatic resources and storage can support longer occupation. A game-scale movement budget preserves actual walking speeds under compressed years.

sources.title: Natural Sleep and Its Seasonal Variations in Three Pre-industrial Societies
sources.finding: Sleep timing varies with season and temperature, begins after sunset, and is not a universal dusk-to-dawn block.
sources.design: Individual chronotype, dawn/dusk and weather influence rest; children and older residents have different daily activity patterns.

sources.title: Why care for someone else's child? Testing adaptive hypotheses in Agta foragers
sources.finding: Non-parental childcare reflects kinship and social cooperation rather than isolated nuclear families.
sources.design: Pooled daily childcare and linked guardians; young children remain with carers rather than independently travelling on adult work routes.

sources.title: Children are important too: juvenile playgroups and maternal childcare in a foraging population, the Agta
sources.finding: Mixed-age playgroups contribute to care and learning.
sources.design: Children's play and gradually increasing chores/learning, not scaled adult work schedules.

sources.title: Twenty Thousand-Year-Old Huts at a Hunter-Gatherer Settlement in Eastern Jordan
sources.finding: Kharaneh IV documents substantial aggregation camps, reused hut spaces and organised activities before farming villages.
sources.design: Long-stay and aggregation camps are possible without forcing every forager group into permanent villages; reused sites can retain hearth and occupation traces.

sources.title: Ohalo II: A 23,000-Year-Old Fisher-Hunter-Gatherer's Camp on the Shore of Fluctuating Lake Kinneret
sources.finding: The lakeshore camp contains multiple brush huts, open-air hearths and specialised activity areas.
sources.design: Real buildable household shelters around shared hearths/work areas; shelter covers follow available techniques/materials and climate.

implementation_status: Research and Core projection checks complete; physical NPC/camp integration in progress, native scene verification not yet accepted. Later landscape and vegetation stages have not started.
